hints: Recall what is special about the isoelectric point, think about the balance of positive and negative charges on the same molecule with no net charge.
walkthrough:
Link isoelectric point to zwitterion**
At its isoelectric point an amino acid has no net charge but it is still ionic inside. The acidic $\text{COOH}$ group has donated its proton to the basic $\text{NH}_{2}$ group on the same molecule. So you get $\text{NH}_{3}^{+}$ at one end and $\text{COO}^{-}$ at the other.

Build valine correctly**
From the Data Booklet, valine has side chain $\text{CH}(\text{CH}_{3})_{2}$ attached to the alpha carbon. Put it together as $^{+}\text{H}_{3}\text{N}-\text{CH}(\text{CH}(\text{CH}_{3})_{2})-\text{C}(=\text{O})-\text{O}^{-}$. Remember to draw out the $\text{C}=\text{O}$ of the carboxylate, not just write $\text{COO}^{-}$.

hints: Start from lysine at pH 9.7 and think about what adding $\text{H}^{+}$ from sulfuric acid does to $\text{COO}^{-}$ and $\text{NH}_{2}$ groups.
Count the basic sites in lysine, there is the alpha amino group plus the side chain $(\text{CH}_{2})_{4}\text{NH}_{2}$ group, plus the carboxylate, and consider stepwise protonation.
For box C at very low pH 1.0, decide the most protonated form possible where every basic site is protonated and the acid group stays as $\text{COOH}$.
walkthrough:
Picture lysine at its isoelectric point**
Lysine is $\text{H}_{2}\text{N}-\text{CH}((\text{CH}_{2})_{4}\text{NH}_{2})-\text{COOH}$ in neutral form, but at pH 9.7 it exists mainly as a zwitterion with overall zero charge. It has three pH sensitive groups: alpha $\text{COOH}$ / $\text{COO}^{-}$, alpha $\text{NH}_{3}^{+}$ / $\text{NH}_{2}$, and side chain $\text{NH}_{3}^{+}$ / $\text{NH}_{2}$.

Add acid stepwise to make 1+ cations**
Lowering pH adds $\text{H}^{+}$. Protonating $\text{COO}^{-}$ to $\text{COOH}$ adds one positive, and protonating $\text{NH}_{2}$ to $\text{NH}_{3}^{+}$ also adds one positive. Any structure with a net single positive charge is a valid intermediate, for example $^{+}\text{H}_{3}\text{N}-\text{CH}((\text{CH}_{2})_{4}\text{NH}_{2})-\text{C}(=\text{O})-\text{OH}$ where the alpha amino is protonated and the acid is protonated, or $^{+}\text{H}_{3}\text{N}-\text{CH}((\text{CH}_{2})_{4}\text{NH}_{3}^{+})-\text{C}(=\text{O})-\text{O}^{-}$ where both nitrogens are protonated but the carboxyl stays ionised. Pick any two different ones for A and B.

Push to pH 1.0 for the fully protonated ion**
At pH 1.0 the solution is strongly acidic, so every base is protonated and the carboxylic acid stays protonated. That gives $^{+}\text{H}_{3}\text{N}-\text{CH}((\text{CH}_{2})_{4}\text{NH}_{3}^{+})-\text{C}(=\text{O})-\text{OH}$ with two $\text{NH}_{3}^{+}$ groups and one neutral $\text{COOH}$, overall charge 2+. This goes in box C.

Final answer: A and B (any two, each with net 1+ charge):
$^{+}\text{H}_{3}\text{N}-\text{CH}((\text{CH}_{2})_{4}\text{NH}_{2})-\text{C}(=\text{O})-\text{OH}$ and $\text{H}_{2}\text{N}-\text{CH}((\text{CH}_{2})_{4}\text{NH}_{3}^{+})-\text{C}(=\text{O})-\text{OH}$ or $^{+}\text{H}_{3}\text{N}-\text{CH}((\text{CH}_{2})_{4}\text{NH}_{3}^{+})-\text{C}(=\text{O})-\text{O}^{-}$
C (pH 1.0, 2+ charge): $^{+}\text{H}_{3}\text{N}-\text{CH}((\text{CH}_{2})_{4}\text{NH}_{3}^{+})-\text{C}(=\text{O})-\text{OH}$

hints: Remember the order Val-Lys means valine provides the $\text{C}=\text{O}$ end and lysine provides the $\text{N}-\text{H}$ end of the peptide link.
Focus on drawing the $-\text{C}(=\text{O})-\text{NH}-$ link fully displayed with all atoms, keeping free $\text{NH}_{2}$ on valine and free $\text{COOH}$ on lysine.
walkthrough:
Set up the condensation the right way round**
Val-Lys is read left to right, N terminus to C terminus. So the $\text{COOH}$ of valine joins to the $\text{NH}_{2}$ of lysine with loss of $\text{H}_{2}\text{O}$. Valine keeps its free $\text{H}_{2}\text{N}-\text{CH}(\text{CH}(\text{CH}_{3})_{2})-$ end, lysine keeps its free $-\text{CH}((\text{CH}_{2})_{4}\text{NH}_{2})-\text{C}(=\text{O})-\text{OH}$ end.

Display the peptide link fully**
Join them with $-\text{C}(=\text{O})-\text{NH}-$. You must show the $\text{C}=\text{O}$ double bond and the $\text{N}-\text{H}$ explicitly. Do not ionise the ends into zwitterions here, draw neutral $\text{NH}_{2}$ and $\text{COOH}$ termini, and leave the lysine side chain as neutral $(\text{CH}_{2})_{4}\text{NH}_{2}$.

Final answer: $\text{H}_{2}\text{N}-\text{CH}(\text{CH}(\text{CH}_{3})_{2})-\text{C}(=\text{O})-\text{NH}-\text{CH}((\text{CH}_{2})_{4}\text{NH}_{2})-\text{C}(=\text{O})-\text{OH}$ with peptide link $-\text{C}(=\text{O})-\text{NH}-$ fully displayed. Accept reverse order Lys-Val if sequence correct for that order.
